## Which file do I need?

Cognitive Terrain runs in your web browser. Nothing to install.

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Play straight away on any computer | **cognitive-terrain-0.22.html**, then double-click it to open in your browser |
| Read the rules | **Cognitive-Terrain-Field-Manual-0.22.pdf** |
| Controls and rules on one sheet, two-sided, to keep by the keyboard | **Cognitive-Terrain-Quick-Reference-0.22.pdf** |
| Run it for a group, build campaigns, see why it works | **Cognitive-Terrain-Practitioners-Manual-0.22.pdf** |
| Hear each week read aloud (optional) | the **Immersive Briefings** voice pack, on its own release: **voice-emma-1** |

Two-player games work as long as both players use a 0.22 build (0.22.0, 0.22.1 and so on).

## What's new

- **Lessons Learned is aimed.** Instead of touching your whole mind, you play
  it on one of your nodes: that node and every node linked to it are pulled
  back a little, lose any framing, and are *trained* for the rest of the
  game, so they recover faster every week and start to come back by
  themselves even once the other side holds them. A node can be trained up to
  three times; a book badge and a ring split into one arc per level mark it.
  The opponent's version works the same way at half strength, and Donovia's
  flooding still lets each one you play shrug off one more attack.
- **Defences you can read at a glance.** A Watch Team or Prebunk now spreads
  like nerves: glowing fibres run from the node it was played on to every
  node it covers, blue for Blue's and red for Red's, with a faint signal travelling outward, tagged with how many
  nodes and how many weeks. They no longer look like the area outlines. The
  same nerves, in your colour, preview what a card would cover before you play
  it, on either mind.
- Two-player codes from 0.21 builds do not work in 0.22.
